Carrier hygiene — director seat (objectstack #12708, session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um), 2026-09-04. `needs:contract-review` removed from this card. Per the maintainer's 2026-08-28 ruling the carrier is never pre-hung: it marks a real reviewable increment (an open PR), and none exists — the card is `pm:blocked` behind #15193 / #15195 / #15196 with no PR (`closed_by_pull_requests` 0). The Clause-② fact stays where it lives, in the card body (a new authoring key `PositionSchema.permissionSets`, four objects retired); the carrier goes on the PR and the card the moment a draft PR opens. Labels rewritten read-modify-write, every other label untouched.

**Pointer added after this card was written: the sharing-rule recipient population gained a member on `main`.**

`SharingRuleRecipientType` now includes **`field`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`), landed by #14103 under the maintainer's ruling B, with the `plugin-sharing` half in flight as #15072 / PR #15235. This card's recipient text was written on 2026-09-04, before that member existed, so its enumeration is one short.

**What it does and does not change for this card:**

- ⛔ **Not an id→name rewrite target.** A `field` recipient's `value` is a **field name on the matched record** — held to the `FieldSchema.name` grammar at parse — not a reference to a catalog item. It is already a name, so the reference-column work this card describes does not apply to it.
- ⚠️ **But it is a recipient, and it expands per record.** Any census, conversion or retirement this card performs over "sharing-rule recipients" must **enumerate it and say what happens to it**, rather than silently covering the members that existed when the card was written. A card that lists five recipient types and meets six is how a member gets dropped.

⇒ Re-derive the recipient population against the then-current `main` when this card is dispatched, exactly as the unlock discipline requires — this pointer is a reason to do it, not a substitute for doing it.

Recorded by the ADR-0131 drafting session (`6679d191-11f4-465b-b322-0e0409d76793`), which wrote this card's body and owes the correction.

The body is not rewritten.**

- `PositionSchema.permissionSets` is still absent, and `spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts:51` carries a closed-shape guidance entry that **refuses** the key. It must be replaced, not just added beside.
- **New consumer of the module:** `delegated-admin-gate.ts` uses `resolveOwnOrganizationRow` (`:720`, `:1105`; #19800). Retiring the module moves that helper, and #21057's direction says the gate's organization match does not change.

  - refusal reporting (#18022, #18088, #18564, #19471);
  - the environment-authored skip (`234d1d8b7c`);
  - provenance locks (#21857, #21881);
  - seed-ownership re-runs (#17872, #21503);
  - the platform-admin audit record (#19194).

**Order:** see #15196's note. The C2/C3 order for `permissionSets` is contradictory and goes to the maintainer.

Ruling: batch #310 items 3, 4 and 7 · letter A · maintainer 「cloud 冻结在 v17 没问题，其他同意你的建议。」 2026-10-10T05:23Z

Director seat, summon #36, `session_019fWAt2renophxLVg5aJXMH` (GitHub `hotlong`; written as `objectstack-fleet[bot]` via the relay). A supplement to the ruling pointer 6094072651 (#22601 B): batch #310 is the seven optimisation items of the ADR-0131 family assessment this seat gave in chat, and the maintainer accepted every item but the cloud one. Three of them are rules the cutover's stage plan carries. Thread-read: 6094072651.

## The three rules

- **Item 3 — one PM owns the cutover.** The cutover batch (this card with C2's S8a, S8b and S9, and the objectui#7611 / pin-bump ordering) is run by an epic PM session on #15194 (`/pm-dispatch epic:#15194`, the skill's Epic 子树车道), not picked stage by stage by the lane seats; that is where C2's fifteen PRs and their hand-offs came from. Until that session sits and posts its delegation record on #15194, no lane seat claims a stage of this batch. S5c on #15196 and C7a on #15211 are outside the batch and stay with their lanes. The summon is the maintainer's.
- **Item 4 — only delete, never fix.** From this ruling to the cutover's landing, a defect in the seven seeders, in `permission-set-projection.ts` or in `per-organization-catalog.ts` is closed `not_planned` with the note "retired by C3 (#15204)", not fixed; no PR touches those modules except to delete them. One exception: a defect that is user-reachable on the current `main` AND lives outside the retired code is a normal card.
- **Item 7 — PR sizing.** The stage plan cuts the batch so that each PR stays under 3,000 changed lines (additions plus deletions, generated files and test deletions included) wherever a clean cut exists: the seeder deletions, the test-file deletions and the object retirements as separate PRs. A PR that cannot be cut under the line is named in the plan with its expected size, so the maintainer can schedule its Tier H approval instead of meeting it in the queue.

## State

- No label change in this act; the triage seat writes the three rules into the stage plan it owes this card (6094072651, item 2), and the epic PM inherits them.

## Seat note: W2 measured a **second cross-tenant write**, through package install · release-cut condition (f) now covers W2 · the refusal is D3's, scoped to catalog-carrying packages · epic PM `session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR` (`marchtian`) · 2026-10-11T22:54Z

**The measurement** (6114807078, on `main` at `3f694715ee`, under `isolated` and `group` alike):
- An organization-A owner holds `manage_metadata` through an org-A-scoped grant (rung `TENANT_ADMIN`, below the operator).
- Through `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`, that owner re-installed an operator-installed package at a new version, adding `manage_users` to its permission set `w2_op_set`. Organization B's member, who holds `w2_op_set`, resolved `manage_users` at the next resolution.
- The same owner then sent `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:id`. The set left the catalog, and B's member lost it.

The gate is `requireInstallCapability` (`manage_metadata`), with no posture rung. Shadowing a name held elsewhere is refused (`Security catalog name conflict`, 422). **Upgrading or uninstalling the package that holds the name is not refused.** The `/api/v1/packages` door installs no catalog items: its manifest has no position or permission-set collections, and catalog writes into a writable package go through `/meta`, which #22895 refuses.

**Release-cut condition (f)** (6113841670) now reads: stage W (#22895) **and W2**. The 17.7.0 exposure of `install-local` is being read now.

**The ruling, within ADR-0131 D3.** D3: "tenant admins cannot create or edit catalog items; the operator defines the catalog for every tenant (managed packages, Studio)". A package that declares positions, permission sets or capabilities is the operator's instrument. So under `group` / `isolated`, below the operator rung (and not `isSystem`), `install-local` refuses:
- **an install** whose incoming version declares any catalog item;
- **an upgrade** where either the installed or the incoming version declares any;
- **an uninstall** of a package whose installed version declares any.

The whole package is refused; a partial install is not well-formed (W2 summary point 5). It uses the same predicate, `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, at the same rung, with the same `403` envelope as the door's sibling refusals. Under `single`, and for a package with no catalog item, nothing changes.

**Not decided here.** Whether a walled organization's `manage_metadata` may install packages at all, or author the environment's objects, views and flows, stays with the maintainer. It is the same open question as W's acceptance notes, and W2 adds the package face of it.

**Build:** stage W2 starts after #22895 lands, so it imports the predicate from `main`.
- Branch: `claude/issue-15204-wall-package-refusal`, based on `main`.
- Pins: the three measured cross-tenant edges, each refused under both walled postures, with the operator, `single` and catalog-free-package controls.
- It also measures the not-yet-measured `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` of a writable runtime package that holds operator-authored catalog items, and refuses it the same way if it is reachable.

- `duplicate`: A's copy re-declares the operator's set unnamespaced. `GET /meta/permission/:name` then serves A's frozen copy.
- `revert` (discard drafts): A discards the operator's pending catalog draft.
- `adopt-orphans`: A adopts environment sets into its own package.
